subject: FinEdge Dedicated: integration & capacity follow-ups
messages:
From: Alyssa Kline <alyssa.k@finedge.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv.menon@finedge.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap & integration asks

Hi Vanessa / team,

Thanks for the demo this morning — good session. Quick recap and a handful of follow-ups from our engineers so we can scope Dedicated correctly:

1) SDK & auth
- We plan to integrate via your Python SDK initially; engineering asked about API key vs mTLS support and sample code for token refresh flows.

2) Routing & fallbacks
- We need to understand traffic shaping: can we route low-latency traffic to a pinned model while sending batch-heavy jobs to a cheaper variant? How does fallback behave when capacity is saturated?

3) Structured output / tool-calling
- Our annotator service will rely on tool-calling for DB lookups and a structured JSON response. Any demo code that shows tool calling + schema enforcement would be helpful.

4) Embeddings / reranking
- We expect ~30k embeddings/day and plan to run reranker stages on top of candidate sets. Curious about recommended batch sizes and whether embeddings can be colocated with the reranker to reduce cross-network cost.

5) Dedicated sizing & autoscale
- Early estimate: 10 qps sustained for text-generation peaks up to 40 qps for short prompts; concurrency spikes up to 200 concurrent sessions during morning batch windows. We need guidance on queue sizing and burst capacity — what buffer do you recommend?

Attached: "finedge-integration-asks.xlsx" with example workloads and traces.

High-level ask: can Redwood provide a short (60-min) architecture deep-dive for our infra + procurement next Wed (6/17)? We want to lock on a mutual action plan and get a draft sizing so procurement can start the reserved-capacity discussion.

Thanks,
Alyssa Kline
Product Manager, FinEdge
Alyssa Kline | FinEdge

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & integration asks

Hi Alyssa — great to meet you and thanks for the detailed workbook, that helps a lot. Quick responses inline and proposed next steps below.

SDK & auth
- Redwood SDKs support API keys and mTLS. For short-lived credentials we also support a token-exchange flow (STS) tied to customer KMS. I'll add a short example for Python token refresh to the drive link and paste the snippet in the architecture call.

Routing & fallbacks
- Yes: routing policies can pin traffic by route or token to a particular model variant. When capacity is constrained you can configure automatic fallback to a compatible quantized variant or to a cheaper region. Fallbacks are per-request and preserve KV prefixes when compatible.

Structured output / tool-calling
- We have a sample that chains tool calls and validates structured JSON against a schema; Marcus will paste a minimal example in the follow-up.

Embeddings / reranking
- Embeddings can be colocated with the reranker if you deploy both on the same Dedicated pool; that reduces cross-network hops. Recommend batch sizes of 64–256 for embeddings depending on sequence length; reranker batches vary (8–32) because of cross-attention overhead.

Sizing & autoscale guidance (high level)
- For 10 qps sustained and 40 qps peaks, recommend a baseline pool sized for 12–15 qps (safety headroom) with burst capacity to 50 qps. Queue depth: start with concurrency queues that hold ~2x peak concurrency to avoid immediate request drops, and tune after observing latencies. Sergio will produce a numeric proposal.

Next steps
- We can run a 60-min architecture deep-dive on Wed 6/17 at 11:00 PT — tentative.
- I'll attach a short PDF proposal with initial Dedicated sizing estimates.

I'll circulate Marcus and Sergio's notes before the call.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Procurement / SLA questions ahead of sizing call

Thanks Rajiv — I'll get procurement-oriented collateral ready. A few technical clarifications that will help us produce a precise Dedicated proposal: 

- Workload details: the workbook showed short prompts (~30 tokens) and longer validation prompts (~400 tokens). Can you confirm percent split and typical response sizes per route? Even ballpark percentiles are fine.
- Concurrency model: are the 200 concurrent sessions full model-attention work, or mostly KV-cache reuse for short-turn dialogues? If KV reuse is high we can significantly reduce memory footprint per session.
- Retry semantics: what retry behavior do you expect for queued requests? Do you prefer immediate retries vs client backoff?

Preliminary sizing notes (rough):
- Baseline pool: 3 x g-p6 equivalent nodes (~12–15 qps depending on prompt length) for sustained 10 qps.
- Burst / autoscale: allow autoscale to add 2 nodes with a 30s scale-up time and 5 min cooldown; configure a priority queue for latency-critical traffic that bypasses long batch queues up to N tokens.
- Concurrency limits: set per-connection concurrency to 8 and per-pool concurrency soft limit at 250; tune after two days of traffic.

Action: I'll upload a short config template (queues + autoscale policy + example policies for fallback) to the drive and paste the link. Also attaching the workload matrix you sent with small annotations.
